stop_condition: Every acceptance criterion in the spec is traced to evidence I reproduced myself, and no unresolved finding at or above high remains in the gate machinery (run-tests.sh store canary, verify-before-stop.sh continuation block, qa-gate.sh request assembly).

findings.evidence: REPRODUCED AGAINST THE SHIPPED RUNNER, not a mutant. I built a fixture L1 tree (mktemp, never production) with a seeded bd store and one spec that genuinely writes to the protected store but derives its target id AT RUNTIME (reads it from a file) instead of naming it literally in its own source. Probe script: scratchpad/probe-derived-id.sh. Result, shipped run-tests.sh, CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR pointed at the fixture: RUN_RC=0; verdict line 'zz-derived-contaminator.sh: PASSED but DEGRADED (1 assertion(s) in 1s; protected store moved but externally attributed to username on fx-ba5)'; summary 'Total: 69  Passed: 69  Failed: 0'; 'Degraded (external store writer during the run - spec(s) NOT failed): 1'. Before dhh7 this exact spec failed the tier (STORE_WRITES -gt 0 was an unconditional FAIL). THE ACTOR FIELD HAS ZERO DISCRIMINATING POWER: I read the fixture's dolt log directly - '8ukmc49um09clj82sh7s06stjp3phpci bd: comment (auto-commit) by username [fx-ba5]' - that commit was written BY THE SPEC ITSELF and is attributed to 'username', the same git user.name a genuine concurrent agent write carries on this host. So of the two tests in the function header's decision rule, the first (does the message carry actor+issue) is only a READABILITY check, and the entire discrimination rests on the source-grep. The header presents the grep as sound on an n=1 generalisation ('the one confirmed self-contamination on record wrote its target id BECAUSE its own source named it') and asserts 'A spec has no legitimate reason to name any real production issue', which reads as complete but does not cover a spec that never names it. 13h/13i are genuine and load-bearing - I verified the sed stub targets attribute_store_advance's own final decision and that 13i runs the unmutated runner over the SAME spec - but their contaminator writes its id literally into the spec via an unquoted heredoc, so they only ever exercise the caught case. SCOPE, measured not assumed: a spec that CREATES in production is still caught - 'bd: create fx-ba5' is the bare-id no-actor shape and takes the ext_ok=0 branch. The gap is exactly the write-to-an-already-existing-id shape, which is the ordinary shape in this repo (specs routinely capture an id from 'bd create --json | jq -r .id' and then write to it; the ten docs/reviews leftovers in this very tree carry mktemp-derived task ids of exactly that form). VERIFIED REMEDY, not a guess: bd 1.2.2 documents '--actor string  Actor name for audit trail (default: $BEADS_ACTOR, git user.name, $USER)'. I tested it in the same fixture - 'BEADS_ACTOR=l1-spec-probe bd comment fx-ba5 ...' produced 'e15cre6mmgkijsj6sh9upeaekclv5ub7 bd: comment (auto-commit) by l1-spec-probe [fx-ba5]'. Exporting a per-run marker into each spec's subprocess environment turns the actor into a real discriminator (marker present = provably this tier's spec = FAIL; absent = provably external = DEGRADED) and retires the source-grep heuristic entirely.
findings.description: The canary has become a partial bypass for the contamination shape that is most common in this repo. It is not silent - DEGRADED is printed and the writer is named - but the tier EXITS 0, so CI goes green, and the whole point of j7kk's canary was an exit-code-bearing structural guard ('nothing here would notice until someone went looking for 9,937 comments by hand'). This is the failure mode the batch brief named as the one that matters. Because dhh7 is gate machinery the other three members were measured under, a wrong canary also weakens confidence in their measurements. REQUIRED FIX (either): (a) export a BEADS_ACTOR marker for the spec subprocess and decide on the marker rather than the source-grep - verified available above, and it makes the guard a proof instead of a heuristic; or (b) if the grep is kept for this round, state the residual explicitly in attribute_store_advance's header (a spec writing to an id it does not name in its own source is attributed external) and add a test leg that exercises the derived-id shape, so the gap is a known bound rather than an unstated assumption.

findings.evidence: Independently confirmed with my own commands, per the coordinator's request. 'grep -n ^EXPECTED_SPECS= .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh' -> '1018:EXPECTED_SPECS=69'. The runner's OWN discovery query, copied verbatim from run-tests.sh:1159-1165, 'find .claude/scripts/tests -maxdepth 1 -type f -name *.sh ! -name run-tests.sh | wc -l' -> 71. I also confirmed 71 is the right number rather than 69 plus two files that should not be discoverable: both new specs are independently verified DISCOVERABLE by that exact query (each matched an exact-line grep of the query's own output), and both are real spec files, not helpers - next-work.test.sh runs 75 assertions and review-request-build.test.sh runs 61, measured by me below. The floor compares with -ne, not -lt: run-tests.sh COMPLETENESS-FLOOR block reads 'if [ $TOTAL -ne $EXPECTED_SPECS ]; then ... finish 1'. So 71 != 69 is a hard tier failure, not a warning. It is invisible to everything run so far because the same block DISARMS the floor under --filter ('Completeness floor: DISARMED (--filter run...)') and all four agents plus the in-session gate runs were filtered or standalone. CI runs it unfiltered: .github/workflows/test.yml:263 'run: bash .claude/scripts/tests/run-tests.sh'.
findings.description: The delivered change set adds two spec files and does not move the counter that pins the discovered set, so the next full L1 run and the next CI run both go red. REQUIRED FIX: EXPECTED_SPECS=71, with the per-change ledger line the constant's own comment block convention demands (naming both new specs and what each is for) - the comment block is explicitly an audit ledger for exactly this number and prior reviews have enforced that convention on it. ON THE WIDER QUESTION the coordinator asked (is there a THIRD single-line whole-tree counter four parallel agents would each have needed to bump): I swept and found NO third one. The only other cross-file invariant inside this batch's blast radius is the EBF-CORE region, which must be byte-identical across qa.md (wuu8 edited) and backend/frontend/devops.md (90av edited) and is pinned by evidence-before-fix.test.sh - I extracted the region from all four and it is INTACT, 5180 bytes with identical sha256 prefix ea08927d29e8a1a7 in every copy. The fixture mirrors are the other one and they are clean (189/189, re-measured below). workflow-manifest.sh deliberately excludes .claude/scripts/tests/ (its own comment at :280 says maxdepth is what keeps it out), so no manifest row is owed for a new spec, and no doc carries a spec count. I also checked the adjacent SPEC_TIMEOUT_S headroom figure, which this repo has let go stale three times: it is NOT invalidated here - the two new specs run in 26.90s and 30.43s against a documented worst case of 771.35s.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/verify-before-stop.sh:8231-8232 (the continuation block) read against the H3 circuit breaker at :3813
findings.evidence: The structural safety claims all CHECK OUT and I verified each mechanically rather than trusting the header. Ordering by line number: the H3 breaker is at :3813 ('if [[ $STOP_HOOK_ACTIVE == true ]]; then echo {}; exit 0; fi'), the release gate 'if [ $QA_APPROVED = false ]' opens at :7850 and its emit_block is at :8048 with the block closing at :8049, so nothing falls through to the continuation block with QA unapproved; NEXT_WORK_DECISION is initialised to 'none' at :8061; compute_next_work is called once at :8113 inside the confirmed-active-epic branch; the continuation block at :8231 fires only on the literal value 'ready'; and emit_block (:3796) ends in 'exit 0' after printing decision:block, so it cannot release. Three-way outcome verified by EXECUTION, not inspection: I ran next-work.test.sh standalone - 75 passed, 0 failed, rc=0, 26.90s - which drives all three arms end to end through the real hook, including A4 (malformed JSON), A5 (a real hang past a real short timeout via the watchdog fallback), A7 (bd not on PATH), C4.5 ('nothing output never claims DEGRADED') and C6 (blocked-only queue renders NOTHING, never ready, and the blocked ids never appear as a delegation target). A bd failure yielding an empty queue does NOT render as done. THE UNDISCLOSED PART: the header argues constraint 1 at length but never addresses what complying with the directive does to the NEXT task. Per this file's own comment at :3810, 'when stop_hook_active is true Claude is already in a forced-continuation state from a previous block', so the Stop event that ends the continuation chain no-ops. C5.0 tests that the breaker holds when fed stop_hook_active:true, but nothing tests or documents the consequence.
findings.description: THE GATE IS NOT WEAKENED FOR THE TASK UNDER REVIEW - I could not construct a path where the continuation block reaches an unapproved task, and it cannot manufacture an approval, only refuse to end a session that already released. What is undisclosed is downstream: the directive's whole purpose is to get more work done in the same chain, and if the :3810 assertion about stop_hook_active holds across that chain, the work done in response lands in a window where the Stop-time technical checks (test/lint/type) will not re-fire. This property is inherent to the H3 breaker and predates 90av - every pre-existing emit_block has it - so this is not 90av inventing a hole. What is new is that 90av is the first block that fires on the APPROVED path and actively invites further work into that window, which changes how often it is exercised from incidental to routine. Not a blocker. REQUESTED: a short note in the NEXT-WORK header naming the interaction and its bound (exposure is one continuation chain; a new user turn re-arms), so the next reader does not have to rediscover it. I am flagging the assumption rather than asserting the behaviour: I could not find an authoritative upstream statement of stop_hook_active's cross-turn lifetime (the hooks reference page I fetched does not contain the field at all), so the claim rests on this file's own :3810 comment. If that comment is itself unverified, that is worth settling on its own.

findings.evidence: MEASURED ON THE REAL PACKET FOR THIS VERY REVIEW, which is the first time the shipped command has been run against a production-scale change set rather than a synthetic. 'qa-gate.sh review-request-build claude-workflow-plugin-gytz --iteration 1 ...' returned ok:true with bytes=286308, diff_bytes=226467, impact_summary_bytes=1433. The configured cap is max_request_bytes=100000 (.claude/review-config, read directly). So the assembled request is 2.86x the cap and THE DIFF ALONE IS 2.26x THE CAP - the diff busts the budget on its own, independently of the completion contract I supplied. codex-review.sh:164-165 refuses at that size with exit 7 before any paid Sol call. THE wuu8 FIX ITSELF IS VINDICATED BY THE SAME MEASUREMENT AND I WANT THAT ON THE RECORD: the impact report on disk is 2,732,721 bytes and the summariser rendered it to 1,433 bytes, 0.5% of the packet - the 98.5%-domination defect the task was filed for is comprehensively fixed. The problem is that with the impact report no longer dominating, the uncapped diff now does, at 79.1%.
findings.description: The in-code rationale for leaving the diff uncapped is that 'the assembled request's own downstream consumer already enforces review-config's max_request_bytes against the REQUEST AS A WHOLE, loudly and by exact byte count'. That consumer exists only in the codex lane; in the claude lane nothing size-checks the request at all, so the justification is lane-asymmetric inside a file that plan correction 10 requires to be lane-agnostic. More practically, the measurement above means the Sol lane is unusable for a change set of this size: the operator has ruled that Codex should be fixed and working and asked for the first genuine dual-family review of this arc, and this packet cannot be delivered. The code is behaving exactly as designed and the refusal is honest - I am not asking for the cap to be removed or for a silent truncation, which the comment correctly rejects. I am reporting that the 'open design question (wuu8)' of whether an oversized diff should be chunked or summarised rather than refused outright is no longer open in practice: it is the live blocker on the dual-family review, and it needs an owner. NOTE ON THE LANE-AGNOSTICISM ARGUMENT THE BRIEF ASKED ME TO JUDGE - I judge it SOUND and the implementer chose correctly rather than cheaply. review-request-build reads no lane, calls no codex-detect/codex-review, and enforces no lane-specific budget key; qa.md runs 6p.1 BEFORE the 6p.2 lane branch; and the claude lane genuinely consumes the request, because three mandatory artifact fields (reviewed_hash, risk_threshold, stop_condition) are specified as copied from it. If Codex vanished, assembly would still be needed and would still work - only the handoff would go. reviewer-lane-structural.test.sh passes 16/16 with both legs green, including the runtime-output leg on all three gate scripts.

findings.evidence: The gate's own reconcile named these: 'SUBTRACTED 11 git-visible path(s) as already-baselined and NOT covered by changed-files.txt'. I confirmed all 11 were present at session start (they appear in the conversation-opening git status), so the subtraction is correct and this is arrival dirt outside the change set, not lost work. But reading one shows what produced it: docs/reviews/impact-report-approve_XXXXXX_KfqBGyjet7-21e-r1.json carries reviewer_model 'test-model' and reviewed_hash e3b0c442... (the SHA-256 empty-content sentinel), i.e. a spec drove review-record with a mktemp-derived task id and the artifact landed in the REAL docs/reviews/ rather than in its fixture. .claude/test-cmd is dated 2026-08-27 and contains 'cd ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD} && make test-fast'.
findings.description: Pre-existing test-hygiene leak, outside this change set and NOT a reason to withhold approval of it. Worth a follow-up task: a spec that writes a review artifact should have its canonical-path derivation rooted at its fixture, or the leftovers should be swept. Left as-is deliberately for now - deleting them mid-cycle would change the working tree under a review in progress, which is the thing qa.md tells me not to do.

findings.evidence: review-request-build refused the umbrella with error_key missing_completion_contract: 'no --completion-contract-file was given and no recorded COMPLETION v1 payload could be found for claude-workflow-plugin-gytz'. That is correct behaviour - the umbrella has no contract of its own by construction, because the four members each recorded their own. I worked around it by assembling the union of the four member contracts into one file and passing --completion-contract-file, labelled in-payload as a QA-assembled union so no reader mistakes it for an implementer's own statement.
findings.description: Not a defect in wuu8's code. It is a friction point between the umbrella pattern (invented in this batch to avoid binding one task's hash to four tasks' work) and the one-task-one-contract assumption in review-request-build and in approve's completion_record_missing refusal. Worth recording so the next umbrella does not rediscover it: either the umbrella task records a union contract of its own at creation time, or the tooling grows an explicit notion of a multi-member change set. No action needed this round.
